chapters.text:
I began in Coldridge Valley, where there was work to be done and a fair bit beyond it worth looking into. The cold of Dun Morogh caught in my throat, and the pines bowed under their snow. Over it all stood the mountain that holds Ironforge, and the country felt less empty for it. I tramped into Anvilmar and met my first wolves. I had all eight Tough Wolf Meat, with rather more appetite for a cooked supper.

I came back to Coldridge Valley. I did for a Burly Rockjaw Trogg, solid on my feet by the end of it. I hunted down six Rockjaw Troggs. I carried out Talin Keeneye's request with Grelin Whitebeard.

The fight with a Frostmane Troll Whelp left me badly shaken. Stubbornness had carried me a long way, but it was no substitute for sense. Afterwards, I put down fourteen Frostmane Troll Whelps, more of them than was strictly fair. I had Grelin Whitebeard's Journal in my pack. I fitted myself with a Frostmane Leather Belt.

I found myself back in Anvilmar, the country on either side worth a second look. I learned Serpent Sting and Track Beasts. I saw Durnan Furcutter's business through with Marryk Nurribit, with a few more faces to nod to.

In all, I had seen six tasks through. I put ten Ragged Young Wolves and four Burly Rockjaw Troggs on the page, glad to be using a pen. I had been on the road an hour and thirty-five minutes. I rested in Anvilmar, glad to have the weight of my pack off my shoulders.

I was ready to move in Anvilmar. The road was not going to shorten itself out of consideration. I arrived in Coldridge Pass. I smelled the Thunderbrew Distillery before I had properly reached Kharanos. Smoke rose above the houses, where dwarves and gnomes crowded together against the cold, and I felt my shoulders ease at the sight. I fixed my hearthstone at the Thunderbrew Distillery, with rather more hope of an ale on my return. I took up skinning and began to learn leatherworking. I came through my first fight with boars, with fresh respect for what was in their mouths. I collected six Crag Boar Ribs. I made a Handstitched Leather Vest. I equipped a Handstitched Leather Vest, my own work.

I reached the Grizzled Den, my boots having opinions about the distance. I concluded the errand between Loslor Rudge and Hegnar Rumbleshot. When I found my way to Brewnall Village, I hunted down a Leper Gnome, a tidy bit of work, if I say so myself. I tracked down eight Gyromechanic Gears. I took lessons in Arcane Shot, still a long way from a master's bench.

Later that day, I came to Shimmer Ridge and put down a Frostmane Snowstrider. I made camp there, with my kit close and little trust in the night.

I woke in Shimmer Ridge and put my pack in order before going on. I brought down Timber there, a name worth keeping when the ordinary fights had run together. I pushed my skinning up to fifty, my hands slower than my pride. I pulled a Frostmane Scepter from the spoils, a fine thing.

When I walked into Frostmane Hold, I overcame a Frostmane Headhunter, the sort of fight that tells better than it fights. I was able to explore Frostmane Hold. I set foot in Amberstill Ranch, curious what the locals would make of a dwarf. I overcame Vagash.

I headed back to Kharanos, the same ruts in the road as before. I trained in Hunter's Mark and Raptor Strike.

I had done five tasks by the end. I had brought down eleven Leper Gnomes and ten Frostmane Snowstriders over the stretch. After two hours and a half, I was ready for a seat and an ale. I rested in Kharanos, with enough behind me to have earned the pleasure of doing very little.

I began this stretch in Kharanos, curious about the ground beneath the road as well as where it led. When I tramped on to the Grizzled Den, I defeated a Young Wendigo. I found eight Wendigo Manes, pleased to have every piece of it. I had Thorgrim for company.

I made it as far as Gol'Bolar Quarry, where I defeated ten Rockjaw Bonesnappers, not the worst scrap I had been in, nor the best. When I took the road back to Kharanos, I came away knowing Concussive Shot and Mend Pet. I walked on to Amberstill Ranch, keen to put a place to the name. I took Bristle on as my companion. I held my hands toward the fire, glad to let them do nothing useful for a moment. I put an end to a Frostmane Seer. I was left without Bristle beside me, where I had grown used to having company.

The blue water of Loch Modan lay still behind the Stonewrought Dam. I knew dwarves built on a grand scale, but the weight of all that water made me stop and look. I tramped into North Gate Pass, judging the stonework before the people. I found the Stoutlager Inn of Thelsamar beside the loch. After the open hills, its ale and blood sausages interested me more than the distance I had come. I cut down a Mountain Boar. I slept lightly, ready to wake at the sounds around me.

I opened my journal in Coldridge Valley. I could not give Gnomeregan back to my people, but there was a world outside it I wanted to understand. The snow of Dun Morogh glowed blue under the stars, and the lamps in the village windows looked warmer for it. The mountains kept me familiar company in the dark. I finished off six Rockjaw Troggs. I had my first taste of fighting wolves. I gathered eight Tough Wolf Meat, rather distracted by thoughts of supper.

I found my way to Anvilmar. I came away from training with Frost Armor and Arcane Missiles, conscious of how much I had not yet tried. I saw Talin Keeneye's business through with Grelin Whitebeard.

I had completed three tasks, and acquired several questions nobody had asked me to answer. The fighting came to nine Ragged Young Wolves. I had been on the road forty minutes. I set the journey aside in Anvilmar, curious how much clearer the day would look after some rest.

I took up the road in Anvilmar, rather pleased that I had not yet run out of things to wonder about. I made it as far as Coldridge Pass. I smelled the Thunderbrew Distillery before I had properly reached Kharanos. Smoke rose above the houses, where dwarves and gnomes crowded together against the cold, and I felt my shoulders ease at the sight. I carried out Beldin Steelgrill's request with Tharek Blackstone, already thinking of a less awkward approach. I added Frostbolt and Conjure Water to what I knew. I went on equipped with an Apprentice's Robe.

I arrived in Brewnall Village, wishing I could make out a little more of the place. I finished off a Leper Gnome. I recovered eight Gyromechanic Gears.

I reached Frostmane Hold, with more to look at than I had allowed time for. I overcame a Frostmane Headhunter. I survived a Frostmane Headhunter, though I needed a little time before I could call the result useful.

book.epitaph: Pippa died by the hand of a Frostmane Shadowcaster in Frostmane Hold, at level six. An hour and a half lived on this realm, and lived well. Let this book stand for Pippa, now that Pippa cannot.

chapters.text:
I began this stretch in Darkshire, with my plans still looking possible before I had begun testing them. I gave my hearthstone a place of return there. I reached Raven Hill Cemetery, where I finished off a Skeletal Horror, relieved to have room to look about again. I cut down fifteen Skeletal Fiends.

When I came to Brightwood Grove, I put an end to six Nightbane Shadow Weavers, with less breath left than I cared to admit. I began using a Night Watch Shortsword. I went back to Darkshire, curious what lay beyond the next turn. I added Seal of Command, Holy Light and Hammer of Justice to what I knew.

I found my way to the Hushed Bank and carried out Madame Eva's request with Abercrombie, with my feet asking for a pause by the end. I walked into Raven Hill. I died there, leaving more unfinished than I had known how to worry about.

I had finished three tasks. I had brought down three Skeletal Horrors over the stretch. After an hour and fifteen minutes, I was glad to have time to think back instead of hurry on. I rested in Darkshire, with no wish to be useful again until I had stopped aching.

I opened a fresh page in Darkshire, glad to have somewhere to put the things I might otherwise forget. I arrived in Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, where I got the better of a Flesh Eating Worm, glad to find my nerve had held. I had all seven Ghoul Ribs. I slept outside, wishing I had found a softer place to lie.

book.prologue: I should have started this journal long ago. I have done eighty-seven good turns already, and I'm writing this in Duskwood.

chapters.text:
I began in the Valley of Trials, with no one's will in place of my own. What I did with that freedom would be my answer. Heat rose from the red dust of Durotar, as if the ground itself were breathing. This was the land we had claimed, and I meant to learn how to belong to it. I overcame ten Mottled Boars. I brought down Sarkoth. I hunted down twelve Vile Familiars, each one met head on. I had ten Cactus Apples in my pack. I settled what Foreman Thazz'ril needed settled.

At Razor Hill I heard the forge before I saw the drilling. Beyond the barracks, Kul Tiras ships sat off the coast, and I understood why no one in the town ever quite stood at rest. I settled Gornek's business with Master Gadrin, quickly, without wasted effort. I added Rend and Battle Shout to what I knew. I went on equipped with a Rough Leather Vest; I finished off a Scorpid Worker, a worthy enough foe in its way. I gathered eight Scorpid Worker Tails.

A Kul Tiras Marine brought me close to the end. I had work left to do, and no use for a glorious excuse for abandoning it. I saw off ten Kul Tiras Sailors, my blood up longer than the fight deserved.

The tasks came to eight, the last for Gar'Thok. My tally came to nine Scorpid Workers. This stretch had kept me busy for an hour and forty-five minutes. Rest would make the strength I had left useful again. I rested in Razor Hill, where the next deed could wait until I could give it my full strength.

I began again in Razor Hill. What was asked of me deserved an answer in deeds. The drums of Orgrimmar echoed off the spiked walls as I came in. At Grommash Hold I felt the weight of it: a city our people had built for themselves, with no one's chains on it. I made it as far as the Valley of Strength, where I studied Charge and Thunder Clap, one more thing to earn before I could claim it. I concluded the errand between Thrall and Gor the Enforcer. I bedded down, making what rest I could of the place I had reached.

I began in Shadowglen, meaning to watch before I called anything understood. Moonlight silvered the leaves of Teldrassil while owls called overhead. I listened between my footfalls, unwilling to hurry through so much quiet. I encountered boars at close quarters. I hunted down seven Young Nightsabers. I carried out Conservator Ilthalaine's request with Mardant Strongoak, finishing before the light changed. I overcame eight Grells. I faced spiders for the first time, not cruel, only hungry. I found ten Webwood Venom Sacs. I came away from training with Moonfire and Rejuvenation, repeating them in quiet until they came without thought.

Rain scented the houses around the moonwell in Dolanaar. The sentinels kept their patient watch on the road, and I let my guard down a little. I completed Dirania Silvershine's errand with Iverron. I slept beneath the open sky, letting the quiet settle around me.

I rose in Dolanaar after resting in the open, and listened before going on. I put an end to a Nightsaber, hunger being no crime, though it nearly cost me. I had all three Nightsaber Pelts. I collected an Emerald Dreamcatcher. I put on Sentinel Trousers, quiet enough to move unheard.

I had completed seven errands, and found the country less distant for knowing what its people needed. I had faced eleven Webwood Spiders and four Nightsabers. I had been on the road an hour and twenty-five minutes. I rested in Dolanaar, listening while my thoughts grew less insistent.

I went on in Dolanaar, conscious that haste had made older mistakes than mine. The white stone and still pools of Darnassus slowed me without my meaning to. Near the Temple of the Moon the old hush settled around me, and I was home. I found my way to the Temple of the Moon, where I was of use to Mathrengyl Bearwalker. I had learned Bear Form, and felt there was a great deal of the world I would need to learn again. I slept lightly there, listening to the world between moments of rest.

I put down my first words in Deathknell, an account chosen freely rather than another order carried out. Crows called over the crypts of Tirisfal, toward the broken walls of Lordaeron. Night changed little here, though it left me feeling less conspicuous. I went from Undertaker Mordo to Shadow Priest Sarvis; I disposed of a Wretched Zombie, with no more fuss than the matter required. I hunted down eight Mindless Zombies. I put down ten Young Night Web Spiders. I recovered six Scavenged Goods, the count exact, which is more than the request was. I collected twelve Scarlet Armbands. I took instruction in Shadow Word: Pain and Power Word: Shield.

After the tombs, the crooked roofs of Brill looked almost companionable. Around the Gallows' End Tavern my people went about their business, and the town kept going on stubbornness alone. I had all ten Tirisfal Pumpkins, the dark no obstacle to me. I overcame Maggot Eye. I added a Lightweight Chain Robe to my equipment, sturdier than me, which is not difficult.

The seven tasks behind me had given people a use for me. That was not affection, but it had its advantages. I had faced twelve Scarlet Converts and eight Wretched Zombies. I had spent an hour and fifty minutes on it. I settled in Brill, where being still was a choice rather than a condition imposed on me.

I took up the road in Brill. It had not learned to like me, but it had not managed to keep me out either. Green canals ran past the bubbling Apothecarium, deep beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Out of so much that had survived badly, we had made a city, and it was ours. When I walked into the Trade Quarter, I was taught Renew and Mind Blast. I tracked down five Vile Fin Scales, for reasons nobody volunteered. I spent the night with the road behind me for a while.

I took up the road in the Dwarven District, with a little curiosity left over from my worrying. I made it as far as the Trade District. I left Stormwind by air for Sentinel Hill, with a little of the day's hurry falling away beneath me.

Westfall lay dark and quiet, its windmills turning over farms nobody tended any more. A light in a window was rare enough to make me wonder who still dared to keep one. A stone tower stood on Sentinel Hill, and around it the People's Militia had pitched their tents. Farmers who had lost everything queued for soup, and it made me angrier than I expected. I walked into the Dagger Hills, keen to get my bearings before going farther. I put an end to a Defias Pathstalker. I recovered a Mysterious Message, glad to leave the searching behind me.

I headed back to Sentinel Hill and saw Gryan Stoutmantle again, the work behind me. Moonbrook was a ruin after dark, its broken walls black against the sky. Somewhere among the burned houses the Defias were talking, and I kept to the shadows. I dealt with a Defias Pillager, straining to make out each movement. I obliged the Defias Traitor.

When I returned to Sentinel Hill, I told Gryan Stoutmantle the work was done. I joined Thessaly, Brannigan, Rowan and Halvard, glad to have someone within reach. I went back to Moonbrook and saw off an Undead Excavator. I recovered four Miners' Union Cards, taking longer to pick things out in the dark. I gathered Thistlenettle's Badge. Timber props held up the tunnels of the Deadmines, and the air tasted of dust and lamp oil. Somewhere ahead, machinery was hammering, as if the whole hill were being worked from the inside. I got the better of a Defias Miner, with less breath left than I cared to admit; I stood over Rhahk'Zor at last. I tracked down a Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. I was there when Sneed fell; I fought Gilnid and won.

The tunnel opened onto a hidden cove, and in the water lay a full-sized ship, armoured and lined with cannons, built in secret beneath Westfall. I understood then how much VanCleef had been planning. I finished off a Defias Pirate, with no wish to meet that foe on the way back. I tracked down ten Red Silk Bandanas.

Mr. Smite nearly finished me. My hands went on shaking after there was any need for them to move. I lived to see Mr. Smite fall. I came by Smite's Mighty Hammer, had it in use before long and finished off Captain Greenskin. With Edwin VanCleef defeated, I could think about leaving the Deadmines instead of surviving the next encounter. I took VanCleef's head as proof. I brought down Cookie.

That night, I made my way back to Sentinel Hill, glad to know the way for once. By nightfall, I handed in my work to Gryan Stoutmantle and took to wearing Chausses of Westfall. I let Scout Riell know it was done, pleased to have the errand behind me. I flew from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind, glad to see how the places fitted together from above.

I found my way to Cathedral Square, where I made sure an Unsent Letter reached Baros Alexston, curious what would come of the work. I found myself back in the Dwarven District. I reported back to Wilder Thistlenettle and Shoni the Shilent, wishing I could see a little farther ahead. When I arrived in Old Town, I added Cleave and Retaliation to what I knew.

I had completed eight jobs, and found myself remembering the people who had asked for them. I had brought down eight Defias Miners and six Defias Pirates over the stretch. I had spent two hours and a half on it. I settled in the Trade District, with the comfortable feeling of having got somewhere I could stop.
I returned to my account in the Trade District, already wondering which names would turn up again. I slept outside there, wishing I had found a softer place to lie.

book.prologue: I've lost count of the roads behind me. Sixty-four tasks, the people say. I start this journal in Stormwind City.
